title: A Franciscan day at home
hookLine: simplicity, praise for creation, joy with the poor

lines: FRANCIS MOVES IN FOR A DAY.
NO LUGGAGE. THANKS FOR THE SALT.
cards: Give Francis your kitchen for a day, and here's what might change. He wouldn't bring luggage. He'd thank God for the bread before he ate it, and probably for the salt too.
He'd stop at the window to greet the weather by name. He'd ask who on your street is hungry, and want to sit with them, not just send something over.
By evening the house might feel lighter, not because anything was cleaned, but because less was needed. Three weeks with Francis end today, not in Assisi, but at home.

teach.b: A Franciscan day at home has three threads, and you've met them all. The first is simplicity. Francis heard the Gospel tell the apostles to take nothing for the road, and took it literally.
At home that doesn't mean selling the couch. It means asking, one thing at a time: do I need this, or does it need me?
Jesus points to the flowers in Matthew, in the Douay-Rheims: "Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow: they labour not, neither do they spin." The second thread is praise.
The whole Canticle is a list of reasons to thank God: sun, wind, water, fire, earth.

teach.h: PRAISE: TURN SMALL THINGS INTO THANKS.
teach.b: A Franciscan home turns small things into praise: grace before meals, a psalm in the morning, thanks at the window.

teach.h: JOY WITH THE POOR, NOT PITY.
teach.b: The third is joy with the poor, not pity from a distance. Francis wrote that when he went among the lepers, what had seemed bitter was turned into sweetness.
In his Admonitions he ties having little to gladness: where there is poverty with joy, he says, there is no greed and no grasping.

teach.h: THREE THREADS HOLD EACH OTHER UP.
teach.b: The three hold each other up. Simplicity without praise turns grim.

teach.h: CONSIDER THE LILIES OF THE FIELD.
teach.b: Praise without the poor turns comfortable. Joy with the poor, without simplicity, runs out of room at the table.
Franciscans have a short greeting for all of it, which some still write at the end of their letters: peace and good.

how: Lay Franciscans and other Catholics drawn to Francis keep a simple rule of life at home: grace before meals, a short daily prayer such as morning or evening psalms, a simpler way of living, and regular service with the poor.

games.q: what does “a franciscan day at home” mean?
o: a day of strict fasting and silence kept by friars
an open house day when friaries welcome visitors
simplicity, praise and joy with the poor, lived in a house

p: do I need this, or does it need me?
grace before meals, thanks at the window

s: a Franciscan day at home means selling everything you own
it starts smaller: asking, one thing at a time, whether you need it.
Francis wrote that poverty with joy leaves no room for greed
it's in his Admonitions: where there is poverty with joy, there is no greed and no grasping.
Franciscan praise is only for church
the Canticle praises God for sun, wind, water, fire and earth, so a kitchen window will do.

games.q: you want to live like Francis for one day at home. where do you start?
o: give away everything you own before lunch.
let one thing go, praise one thing, and remember one person with less.
read every book about Francis you can find.
games.why: the three threads are small and daily: simplicity, praise and joy with the poor, each holding up the others.

practice: Look around the room and pick one thing you could do without today, the second coffee, the scroll before bed, the purchase in your cart, and let it go, just for today.

Then pick one small thing to praise, the light through the window, the chair holding you, and thank God for it by name if you pray, or just say thank you into the room; last, hold one person with less than you for a breath.

wordCard.voice: A Franciscan day at home. Simplicity, praise for creation and joy with the poor, woven together in an ordinary house. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin: peace and good, a Franciscan greeting some still write at the end of letters.

carryVoice: Your line: praise and simplicity. Three weeks with Francis ran from bitter became sweet and take nothing, through perfect joy and brother wolf, to welcome, sister death and still walking. Tomorrow, Dominic.
